Finding.Text: Evidence recorded by the 0.3.0 kernel does not survive the 0.3.0 to 0.4.0 upgrade, and the documents say it does. The candidate rule changed with this change, not only the pin: 0.3.0 hashed the pin into the candidate and 0.4.0 leaves it out, so every revision that carries a pin has a different candidate under the two kernels. Probed with a scenario pinned 0.3.0 whose start run was recorded by the v0.3.0 checkout: that kernel printed "candidate: 9aca3683 (clean)" and "check CK1: passed, counts"; the 0.4.0 kernel on the same tree, before and after its pin bump and after the pin was committed, printed "candidate: f9e638b8 (clean)" and "check CK1: passed, does not count: recorded on an earlier candidate, recorded with grace5 0.3.0", and close refused "check CK1: recorded on an earlier candidate". A review record written under 0.3.0 is "on an earlier candidate" for the same reason. The kernel is behaving as the new rule says and errs in the safe direction, but the sentences are false for the one transition that exists today: upgrade.md "writing it changes no change's candidate and invalidates no evidence: a change may span kernel versions", the source-identity.md example row "upgrade writes the pin ... Same ... The result still counts; status names the kernel it was recorded with", and the contract's A1 reading of UP-15, which records and reads with the same kernel. The pilot named in Problem, three open changes with evidence and reviews recorded by 0.3.0, will upgrade and find every result and every review stale at once, which is a rerun of every check and a re-review per change; nothing in upgrade.md, source-identity.md, commands.md, README or the two skills says so, and the only hint is the ", recorded with grace5 0.3.0" suffix. CK6 cannot see this because the verifier computes the candidate before the upgrade with the new kernel. The same rule change means the close records already written with the pin included no longer reproduce under this kernel: C-0004's close.xml and review-1.xml name candidate 8907d111 and this kernel gives e4604ae4 for that revision e33e899; C-0001 to C-0003 closed before a pin existed and reproduce (C-0003's d95fd1f1 does); run-1.xml of this change carries 8907d111 by the 0.3.0 rule. No kernel path compares a closed change's candidate, and each record names its kernel, so those records keep their meaning for a reader who applies the rule of the kernel named; this needs saying where the rule is amended. For the owner: either the documents state that the 0.3.0 to 0.4.0 boundary changes the candidate of every pinned tree once, so results and reviews recorded by 0.3.0 are rerun and re-reviewed after it and the closed records of 0.3.0 are read by its rule, or the owner disposes of the cost in quoted words.

The change alters two skills and ships no migration step, against the method's own sentence. method.md (unchanged, line 79) and upgrade.md say "A kernel change that alters the state layout, the ignore lines or the skills ships its migration step in the same change"; the diff changes skills/grace5-execute/SKILL.md and skills/grace5-prepare/SKILL.md (one sentence each, the ways out) and declares the 0.3.0 to 0.4.0 boundary a pin bump, as the contract's Change text says. Skills are refreshed on a step only (applyUpgrade calls refreshSkills inside the step branch; UP-07 now asserts "never per bump"), so a pilot at 0.3.0 with the grace5-* directories installed keeps the 0.3.0 text after upgrading. Probed on a HEAD clone pinned 0.3.0 with the v0.3.0 packaged skills under .agents/skills: upgrade printed the bump, "open, untouched", "pinned: 0.4.0" and "upgraded: 0.3.0 -> 0.4.0" with no refreshed line, and the installed execute skill still reads "run grace5 upgrade first, which needs every change closed", the advice F1 of review 1 of C-0004 called unable to succeed; no kernel facility refreshes it until some later version ships a step. The kernel does what the approved contract says, so the resolution is the owner's: a step for 0.3.0 to 0.4.0 that refreshes the skills (a contract revision; it would list the installed files as writes: and, with F1, cost the pilot nothing it has not already lost), or an amendment of the sentence in method.md (a protected path) and upgrade.md that says when a skills-only change may be a pin bump and what the installed skills are then.

"evidence of open changes becomes history: <id>" is printed whenever --accept-evidence-loss is given with changes open, including when the union of writes is empty and nothing becomes history. Probed on a HEAD clone with the pin removed and committed, C-0005 open and no skills installed: upgrade --accept-evidence-loss printed the line, wrote only the pin, and status afterwards showed the same candidate 19846c16 (clean) with every check still counting. The line then states a cost that is not incurred. commands.md and upgrade.md describe the implemented behaviour exactly, and notes.md says it follows the contract's wording, but the contract ties the line to the case in which the refusal would have come, that is to a pending source write. Printing it only when writes is non-empty would keep every line of the output true.

The start run's CK6 result reads verdict="passed" on the 0.3.0 kernel, before the behaviour it checks existed: the 0.3.0 upgrade-verify.ts ignored arguments it did not know, so "bun src/tools/upgrade-verify.ts --with-open-change" ran the plain verifier, and its log shows the chain to 0.3.0 with no open change laid out. That pass is not evidence of anything the check claims and a reader of the receipt should not take CK6 as a check that passed both before and after. The final tool refuses an unknown argument (probed: "unknown argument --bogus; the only flag is --with-open-change", exit 1), so from this candidate on the flag cannot be ignored. The start receipt is not counted at close, so nothing closes on it; the finding is for the record.

On this candidate it passes, and it fails where the tool's own checks bite: a kernel that refused on the open change, wrote into its directory, announced a write the clone does not need, counted it as closed, or left the untracked pin in the dirty state (the before line is "(clean)" and the after line must equal it with the pin untracked, which is the dirty exclusion). What it proves and what it misses: the candidate hash cannot change in this run because HEAD is never moved and the pin is never committed, so "candidate unchanged" is the dirty exclusion and the hash equality is trivial; the committed-pin half of the exclusion is UP-15 in CK2. The before candidate is computed by the kernel under test, so the run cannot see that 0.3.0 would have hashed the same tree differently (F1). The open change has no receipt, so no result is shown to survive; the refusal paths (a touching step, a pending source write, the flag) are not exercised here but in UP-13 and UP-14, which the reviewer confirmed black-box on a v0.2.0 clone with a stale installed skill. The start-run pass of this check is spurious (F4). Rerun by the reviewer: every ok line, exit 0, the same output as the run-4 log.
Review.Rule: The rule's definition of source and of the candidate is amended in the one place K1 names, the pin joining the excluded paths, and the prose and two example rows describe that amendment; the kernel follows it in one function, isSource, used by candidateOf, dirtyPaths and changedBetween, excluding the exact pin path and nothing else (probed: a sibling file under .grace5/ and .grace5/kernel-version.bak are source; the conformance helper's independent computation agrees in UP-15). Writing, removing or committing the pin changed no candidate and no dirty state in every probe. Without --accept-evidence-loss an upgrade with open changes present writes nothing a candidate reads: the two refusals come before the plan and before any write (porcelain unchanged after each), and a proceeding upgrade wrote only the pin; with the flag it writes the listed source paths and says so. It never writes under an open change: touches is read before anything is written, a declared open id refuses with no override, and the kernel's two steps declare only the closed siblings the move takes and nothing else, so the kernel cannot reach that refusal by itself and the runner test covers it. The start run recorded the start revision and the diff for this review runs from it; the kernel stages, stashes and commits nothing. One sentence the file now carries is false for results recorded under 0.3.0, because the amendment itself changes the candidate of every pinned tree once (F1); the rule as a definition is upheld and the kernel conforms to it.

The diff amends exactly one entry, L-23, and adds none. The amendment reaches four columns, not the two K3 names: mechanism (the pin outside the candidate, the narrowed refusal, the source-write refusal and its override), source (the owner ruling of 2026-11-13 after the lockout, which matches D1 and is a kind the ledger admits), expected benefit (a change may span kernel versions) and cost (the declarations per step, the flag, the verifier run with an open change); the wider amendment is what the ledger's own columns require once the source changed, and the removal criterion stands. The flag and the declarations are recorded as cost of the upgrade mechanism rather than as mechanisms of their own, which is consistent with how L-23 already folded the pin and the command into one row. The candidate rule's own entry, L-09, is unchanged although the rule was altered; the exclusion exists for the pin's sake and L-23 names it, so one entry carries it, as the rule allows.
